problem: RL-based target-object visual navigation policies learn generic obstacle avoidance and search, and often fail to complete the task even when the target is within reach. Delayed rewards make credit assignment hard, and model-based RL is data hungry.
motivation: A model-free RL agent has no explicit notion of which future state leads to success. The value function is its only signal about the future, and it is unused at test time. Giving the agent an imagined latent (sub-)goal state could provide foresight without modelling full environment dynamics.
key_idea: Train a plug-in module (FSI) that, from the initial state and target embedding, imagines in the policy's shared LSTM latent space the sub-goal state most attended in successful trajectories, and condition the on-policy A3C policy on that noisy imagination.
insight: The gain comes from imagining a meaningful sub-goal, not from extra input. Random imagination (Ours-RND) slightly hurts (SR 64.8 vs 65.3), and predicting the attention-weighted average of states (Ours-ATT) gives only marginal gain (65.4). Imagining once from the initial state beats imagining at fixed intervals (Ours-INT, SR 63.8), which the authors attribute to policy collapse. Gains are larger on long trajectories and in kitchen/living rooms, consistent with imagination countering LSTM forgetting and aimless wandering.
method: Sub-goal selection: the value function is computed on a residual attention over past states (query/key/value linear maps). The state with maximum attention weight at the end of a successful trajectory is taken as the sub-goal.

Imagination network f_w: a 6-layer tanh MLP with a bottleneck maps [s_0; target embedding] to the sub-goal latent. It is trained with a smooth L1 loss on a small replay buffer of successful trajectories (size 32, emptied after each update).
Shared state space: the LSTM state encoder is shared by policy and imagination, so the imagined latent implicitly encodes the trajectory history leading to the sub-goal.

Imagination-conditioned policy: pi(a|s_t, g, i), where i is the imagined state plus Gaussian noise. The noise variance is max(sigma_max^2 - moving success rate, 0), with sigma_max^2 = 0.9 and a 100-episode window, so exploration decays as success grows.

A3C integration: actor and critic losses use the attended value V(s~_t). Each asynchronous worker keeps its own buffer and imagination copy, and the weights are transferred to the shared model after each update. No pre-exploration is needed.

setting.backbone: ResNet-18 features + 1-layer LSTM (512) + A3C actor-critic with FSI MLP (trained from scratch, ResNet-18 pretrained); baselines SAVN (MAML) and ORG (Faster R-CNN detections + graph)
setting.training_data: RL in AI2-THOR: 20 training scenes per room type (4 room types), 5 val, 5 test; no extra data
setting.observation: egocentric RGB (ResNet-18 features) + target object embedding (GloVe; one-hot in setup 2)
setting.action_space: discrete low-level: RotateLeft, RotateRight, MoveAhead, LookDown, LookUp, Stop

numbers.extra: MAML test-time adaptation as in SAVN

numbers.backbone: ResNet-18 + LSTM A3C + Faster R-CNN object graph (ORG)
numbers.extra: off-the-shelf object detector; no imitation learning

numbers_note: Benchmarks are the AI2-THOR ObjectNav setups of SAVN and ORG, not a canonical name. Ablation table (Ours-FSI 38.66 SPL / 67.6 SR) differs from main table numbers for the same model. Per-room results are in a separate table.
results: FSI improves every baseline: A3C SR 33.04 to 36.80, A3C+MAML 40.86 to 45.5, and A3C+ORG 65.3 to 68.0 (SPL 37.5 to 39.41). Gains are larger on trajectories over 5 steps and on kitchen and living room scenes.
limitations: Gains are modest (about 2-5 SR points) and evaluated only in AI2-THOR against A3C-style baselines.
Imagination is trained only on successful trajectories; failures are not used. A single sub-goal is imagined from the initial state, which may be hard in large or unseen scenes.
Bathroom SPL dropped slightly in both setups.
